questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Living in a country outside of Europe

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was decent. At some points it was a bit confusing but overall okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UCSC had provided semi detailed information about my move in, student life, financial aid possibilities etc. before my arrival which helped a lot.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: KU did facilitate a few introduction meetings and had created a timeline and "to dos" the months before the studying abroad but didn't provide any detailed information about further assistance, practical about the destination's University, attached advisors, structure etc. This was only provided by UCSC which also makes sense in some ways but I could have wished for more clearance and support from KU.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to be almost guaranteed housing on campus and had to apply for all their different options prior to the move in.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I could apply for housing either in apartments or in dorms. In the dorms you wouldn't have any kitchen available which made the meal plan mandatory. If you lived in an apartment you had a kitchen available (you and your flatmates are required to provide kitchen tools yourself) which is why you weren't required to be a part of the meal plan. You are able to get a small discount for the dining halls/mealplans if you wished for this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive! And you have to be prepared to live close with your flatmates unless you are living in a single room. But housing on campus is convenient and safe - at UCSC you live close to other exchange students and close to the classrooms. I did also chose to move out and live off campus for one quarter which was also very nice! But it requires a bit more responsibility and awareness for potential spam as well as more move out preparation. But I would recommend both types of housing!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is pretty easy when you first understand the system. You can prior to your enrollment date get an orientation of the course options and try to create your own schedule.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. You receive a mail with an enrollment date. 
2. You have some time to look in a course catalogue  of your options. 
3. You can add the courses to a so-called shoppingcart so you are ready to "purchase" your courses on your enrollment date. 
4. You can create a schedule before final enrollment. 
5. You are able to switch and change courses the first two-three weeks of the quarter if spots are available at the given course - otherwise they have a waitinglist system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Youtube videos and guidelines on their webside

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have the opportunity to select courses outside of your major you should definitely try that out - just for fun and the experience of learning more about other fields/majors.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors and teachers are very sweet, helpful and open minded - especially also towards exchange students but the level of difficulty is very low!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Low and easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to have a lot more assignment, homework, attendance and presentations throughout the quarter but then a "smaller" final/exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had free gym, gym classes and in general good free sports facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can either enroll in sports courses like sruf, tennis, soccer, sailing etc. at the beginning of the quarter or you can choose to sign up for gym classes through the week: Mat pilates, Zumba, Kick boxing, Yoga etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf of sailing classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the national parks and other cities around your own.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit overwhelming but easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Classic one but be open minded and trust the process.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: language, young ages, study structure, the students lack of indepence.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The American's open minds, small talks and inclusitivity.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to meet many new different people - maybe a bit of a culture shock -, study on a campus with beautiful nature and have a good amount of savings for trips!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to go alone without knowing any.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
That not all americans are weird and support Trump
lol...And
ofc all the wonderful trips and experiences!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I went on my own without knowing any and that I did not hang that much out with other danes now that I was primarally the only one:))

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it! But be prepared to put in a lot of work prior to your start and apply for a lot of scholarships.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
